sessionTitle: Under the hood of Microsoft AI models

announcements.name: Seven new MAI models across image, transcription, voice, coding, and thinking
announcements.shortDescription: Announced at the morning keynote and detailed here model by model
announcements.longDescription: Dave Citron maps out the seven models Microsoft AI announced at the morning keynote, spanning image, transcription, voice, coding, and thinking. Image 2.5 is the image generation/editing model, now #2 on the LMArena [inferred] leaderboard for image-to-image, with a Flash variant at a third of the cost. Transcribe 1.5 is described as the world's most accurate transcription model across 43 languages and 5x faster than rival models; Voice 2 is the most natural-sounding speech model preferred in 72% of blind tests with a sub-150ms Flash variant; Code 1 Flash is a 5-billion-active-parameter coding model shipping as default in GitHub inside VS Code; and Thinking 1 is the first reasoning model scoring 97% on AIME [inferred] and 53 on SWE-bench Pro.

announcements.name: Image 2.5
announcements.shortDescription: Image generation and editing model ranked #2 for image-to-image on the LMArena [inferred] leaderboard, surpassing Nano Banana, with a Flash variant delivering production quality at roughly a third of the cost
announcements.longDescription: Image 2.5 is Microsoft AI's image generation and editing model, ranked #2 on the image editing leaderboard, surpassing Nano Banana. Its standout strength is precision: it executes edit instructions with high fidelity and consistency, handling complex compositional edits such as changing lighting, adding environment-matched objects, and editing one region while leaving the rest intact. The flagship model is optimized for maximum quality and is already live in PowerPoint, rolling out to OneDrive, and available on Foundry, while the Flash variant offers the same architecture tuned for high-volume production with more throughput and significantly lower cost per token. Users are encouraged to try it on the MAI Playground website, even from a phone.

announcements.name: Transcribe 1.5
announcements.shortDescription: Described as the world's most accurate transcription model across 43 languages and up to 5x faster than rival models
announcements.longDescription: Transcribe 1.5 is presented as the best transcription model in the world, with state-of-the-art accuracy across 43 languages, beating Gemini and OpenAI's flagship transcription models on head-to-head accuracy benchmarks. Beyond benchmark accuracy, it is optimized for real-world use including noisy environments, accents, domain-specific terminology, and multiple speakers. On artificial analysis speed benchmarks it is up to 5x faster than rival models while also being more accurate. It is already integrated across the Microsoft stack—Copilot, Teams, GitHub, Dynamics 365—and is available on Foundry now.

announcements.name: Voice 2
announcements.shortDescription: Most natural-sounding speech model yet, preferred in 72% of blind listening tests, with fine-grained emotional control, voice cloning from a few seconds of audio, and a sub-150ms Flash variant for voice agents
announcements.longDescription: Voice 2 is Microsoft AI's latest speech generation model, distinguished by its naturalness through deep work on prosody—the rhythm, stress, and intonation that make speech sound human rather than like a text-to-speech engine. Its headline new capability is fine-grained emotional control, letting users tune not just what the voice says but how it feels (warm, urgent, conversational, joyful), available today in 15 languages with more coming. It also performs high-fidelity voice cloning from just a couple seconds of source audio. A Flash variant designed for voice agents with very low latency is also planned, and the model can be tried on the MAI Playground or in Foundry.

announcements.name: Code 1 Flash
announcements.shortDescription: Efficient agentic coding model with ~5 billion active parameters, scoring 71.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.2 on SWE-bench Pro, shipping as default in GitHub Copilot inside VS Code
announcements.longDescription: Code 1 Flash is Microsoft AI's efficient, dedicated coding model built from the ground up for agentic coding tasks at speed, with just 5 billion active parameters. It scores 71.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.2 on SWE-bench Pro, one of the hardest real-world coding benchmarks, and is optimized to be cost-effective for high-throughput workloads. It is already shipping as the default in GitHub Copilot inside VS Code, where the speaker encourages developers to try it.

announcements.name: MAI Thinking 1
announcements.shortDescription: First Microsoft reasoning model: mixture-of-experts, 35 billion active parameters, ~1 trillion total, 256K context, hill-climbed from scratch with no distillation
announcements.longDescription: Thinking 1 is Microsoft's first reasoning model, given an in-depth look in this session. Its architecture is a mixture-of-experts model with 35 billion active parameters, about 1 trillion total, and a 256K context window, and it punches above its weight class on benchmarks. It was hill-climbed entirely from scratch with no distillation and no teacher model, using clean, commercially licensed data lineage suited for shipping to enterprise customers. Training used 30 trillion tokens processed in house plus another 3.55 trillion tokens of curated STEM, math, and coding data in mid-training, which also extends context to 256K.

announcements.name: 100+ page technical report
announcements.shortDescription: Published on the MAI website detailing how Thinking 1 was built
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft AI launched a technical report on its website the morning of the keynote, giving a detailed, over-100-page account of exactly how Thinking 1 was built from scratch. The report covers the complex architecture and training diagrams shown in the session and is organized around three governing principles: capabilities should be learned not inherited, simplicity is sustainable, and scientific rigor over shortcuts. It details data choices including the avoidance of open-source training sets and synthetic data, and the use of decontaminated benchmarks.

announcements.name: Microsoft Frontier Tuning
announcements.shortDescription: Lets developers and organizations tune models on their own data inside their secure tenant, deploying through Foundry or Copilot
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft Frontier Tuning, announced at the morning keynote, lets every developer and organization build its own hill-climbing machine—a model trained on their own work, language, and data entirely inside their environment, rather than renting a generic model. It emphasizes four things: it is private so data never moves, cost efficient, gets smarter on the user's actual context, and keeps the user in control with no big-model lock-in. The process is to define the task and what good looks like, bring your data and M365, Azure, and Fabric context and workflows, then run training inside your secure tenant, deploying through either Foundry or Copilot. Real usage feeds back into the next training cycle so the model improves the more the organization uses it.
